commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
fix(agent): narrow the Hibernate proxy marker and keep Lombok defaults

Match $HibernateProxy only at the end of the class name so a class such
as Order$HibernateProxyFactory is still instrumented. Drop the $default$
exclusion: a @Builder.Default initializer is the field's own expression
and can hold real logic. Document how long accumulated exports are kept.

commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
fix(agent): drop Hibernate 6, Mockito and builder noise; add accessors=record

Running the agent over a real Lombok/JPA service turned up noise that the
earlier filter missed:

- Hibernate 6 names its proxy Order$HibernateProxy with no suffix.
- Mockito mocks ($MockitoMock$) were recorded as application code.
- Lombok builder methods (store the argument, return this) made up a fifth
  of the reverse index; Lombok's $default$ initializers ran on every build.

Skipping accessors has a cost: a class made only of them, such as a
request DTO record, disappears from impact analysis. accessors=record keeps
them for a CI recording; on that service it cut unmatched changed files
from 33 to 21 over the last 12 commits. The default is unchanged.

commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
fix(starter): keep every test context's requests in the exported report

Spring's test context cache keeps one application context per distinct
test configuration and closes them all at JVM exit. Each context's
ReqoverReportExporter overwrote the same file, so the report covered only
whichever context closed last. Applied to a real Spring Boot service
(167 tests, five contexts), the report listed 20 of the 50 endpoints the
tests called.

Exports to one path in the same JVM now accumulate. The first export of a
run still replaces the file, so an earlier run never leaks in. The request
id sequence is JVM-wide so the merged report does not repeat req-1.

Document attaching the agent to the test JVM in the CI guide.

commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
chore: store gradlew.bat with LF in the index

The gradle-wrapper bump committed gradlew.bat with CRLF in the index.
.gitattributes converts *.bat to CRLF only in the working tree, so every
fresh checkout showed the file as modified.

commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
fix: drop proxy, accessor and unmapped-URL noise from reports

Attaching Reqover to a real Spring Boot service (a Lombok-heavy MVC app)
showed three kinds of noise that buried the code that matters:

- Runtime proxy classes (`$$SpringCGLIB$$`, `$HibernateProxy$`,
  `$ByteBuddy$`) live in the application's package, so an include
  matched them and every proxied service was listed next to its own
  `$$SpringCGLIB$$0` twin. AgentOptions now always excludes them; the
  real method behind the proxy is still recorded.
- Trivial accessors run whenever Jackson serializes the object, so a
  shared response envelope's getters topped the reverse lookup as "used
  by every API". TrivialAccessorScanner finds methods whose whole body
  reads or writes one of the class's own instance fields, by bytecode
  shape rather than by name, and the instrumenter skips them. A getter
  that computes anything is still recorded.
- Spring Boot maps a static resource handler to `/**`, so every URL that
  matched no controller piled up under one `GET /**` endpoint. The MVC
  interceptor and the WebFlux filter now skip requests served by
  ResourceHttpRequestHandler / ResourceWebHandler.

On that service the busiest endpoint went from 19 classes / 62 methods to
8 / 15, and the top shared method in the reverse lookup went from a
response getter to the domain rule that three APIs really share.

The WebFlux agent E2E test proved the parallel-thread hop through the
response record's accessors only. The sample now maps through a
`toResponse` method, and the test asserts both that method and that the
record's accessors are no longer recorded.

commits.message:
refactor(core): drop the unreachable eviction-policy parser

Spring's relaxed binding already turns `oldest-first` and
`reject-when-full` into the enum constants, so `fromProperty` had no
caller in main and was a second parser that could drift from the first.
It also lower-cased with the default locale, which turns `OLDEST_FIRST`
into `oldest-fırst` under tr_TR and throws.

While finishing the review of #15: the Korean integration guide gets the
same two property rows and the retention paragraph, the changelog
records the feature under Unreleased, the English guide stops attributing
the policy to 0.2.0, and the two configuration classes lose a trailing
blank line.

commits.author: lsmin3388
commits.message:
docs(perf): replace the retired measurement with one that has a slope

The 2026-08-10 capture reported the agent as faster than the baseline,
which is what a single-order run produces when drift points the same way.
It is retired rather than reinterpreted.

Measures four endpoint shapes over six alternating rounds each. At four
instrumented entries the cost is inside the noise floor; at a thousand
and above every round agrees, giving about 24 ns per instrumented method
entry. Lists what the measurement does not cover — concurrency, GC,
startup — because those are where a surprise would come from.

Adds a roadmap, so the order we intend to work in is arguable in public.
